messages:
sara_support: Customer hit intermittent 502s + high tail latency earlier today. They gave a request_id: `req_20260318_6a2b9f11`. Can someone search server logs for that id and confirm which service returned 502 and whether any upstream timeouts happened? Also: what's our log retention for these request-level traces?

miguel_sre: got it — can you paste the exact request_id from the customer (no truncation)? Also useful: their org_id and an approximate timestamp (timezone). Retention quick note: hot request logs (gateway + edge) are in ELK for 30 days; full debug bundles are kept for 14 days in the archive. If the event is older than 30d we need an archive extraction.

sara_support: full id is `req_20260318_6a2b9f11` (same). Customer timestamp: 2026-03-18T14:08:22Z, org_id: `org_82c7`. They also provided a curl repro that hits /v1/generate and gets 502 at ~3s.

sara_support: curl snippet they gave:
```
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-customer' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"gpt-small","input":"hello"}'
```

miguel_sre: searching ELK now. KQL to run (copy/paste into Kibana Discover against logs-* index):
```
request_id.keyword: "req_20260318_6a2b9f11" OR trace.id: "6a2b9f11"
```
Look for `http.response.status_code`, `upstream.error` and `latency_ms` fields. If you can't find it, also try `message: req_20260318_6a2b9f11` because some older components emit it only in freeform logs.

james_infra: if we need raw host logs (container stdout) here's a quick helper we use (requires support-prod role):
```bash
# fetch from internal log service (auth via OIDC token)
TOKEN=$(aws ssm get-parameter --name /support/prod-token --query Parameter.Value --output text)
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 
  "https://internal-logs.redwood:9200/_search?q=request_id:req_20260318_6a2b9f11&size=500"
```
This will return host, pod, and exact log lines. Note: results are limited by shard TTL; if empty and within 45 days we can request an archive pull.

miguel_sre: found matches in `gateway-prod` and `edge-parser-prod`. Summary: gateway returned 502 with `upstream_timeout` at host `gw-12` and edge-parser logged `kv_cache_miss` followed by a 1.2s parse step and then an HTTP upstream timeout to model-proxy at ~2.9s. Snippet: "http.response.status_code":502, "upstream.error":"timeout", "latency_ms":2932. I have 6 raw lines; do you want me to paste them or generate a debug bundle?

sara_support: paste masked lines and then request the debug bundle — customer is worried about billing and wants a repro. Mask any API keys. :thumbsup:

miguel_sre: pasted masked lines:
```
[gw-12] req=req_20260318_6a2b9f11 method=POST path=/v1/generate status=502 upstream_error=timeout upstream_host=model-proxy-03 latency_ms=2932
[edge-parser-prod] req=req_20260318_6a2b9f11 stage=parse msg="kv_cache_miss" took_ms=1204
[model-proxy-03] req=req_20260318_6a2b9f11 outgoing_call status=504 target=model-backend-07 elapsed_ms=2800
```
All API keys and user tokens stripped. Looks like model-backend-07 had a 504 to the proxy which bubbled to gateway as 502.

debug-bot: Automated note: debug bundle is available for requests within 14 days. To generate, run: `./support-tools collect-bundle --request req_20260318_6a2b9f11 --out /tmp/bundle.zip` (requires support-prod role).

sara_support: customer wants repro steps and the curl they gave fails consistently in their environment. They also reported spikes of latency regionally. Can we also check if model-backend-07 had any resource pressure around that time?

james_infra: checking metrics now — model-backend-07 had CPU burst + high queue depth at 14:07:xxZ; some worker restarts at 14:06:50Z which correlate with a short GC pause. I'll pull the pod restart logs and include in the bundle. If necessary, we can request extraction of extended traces (X-Ray/Opentelemetry) but those are only stored for 21 days in tracing service.

miguel_sre: action items: 1) I'll generate a debug bundle and upload to the ticket (will scrub secrets). 2) James, can you attach the pod restart logs and CPU traces. 3) Sara, ask customer to capture a curl with `-v` and `-H 'x-request-id: <their-id>'` so we have a matching client-side header. Also ask whether they used a proxy or NAT that might cut connections at ~3s.

sara_support: will ask customer for the verbose curl + confirm network path. I've created support ticket 84721 and will attach your bundle when ready. ETA: Miguel — how long to generate and scrub?

miguel_sre: ~15–20 minutes to generate + scrub and upload. If we need historical archive pulls (older than ELK TTL) allow 2–4 hours.

sara_support: noted. I'll update customer with ETA. Thanks everyone. :raised_hands:
